decisions.executionNote: Wait with both arms stationary and open while observing the opponent's discard.
Continue waiting; the opponent is still moving toward its tiles.
Keep clear until the opponent exposes the discarded tile.
Wait for the pushed tile to settle face up so its matching group can be identified.
Continue observing the opponent; its tile is not yet clearly exposed.
Discard is a bamboo tile matching the three bamboo tiles on the right side of the row. Begin a raised, elbow-up right-arm approach while the left stays clear.
Align the right gripper in front of the leftmost matching bamboo tile, keeping above the upright row and preserving the elbow-up bend.
Close the right gripper to form a narrow pusher, then approach only the first matching bamboo tile's face.
Gently tip the first matching bamboo tile away from the robot with a narrow forward-and-down push; avoid its upright neighbors.
Continue the small forward/down tipping motion on the same bamboo tile; it is still partly upright in the wrist view.
Lift and retract the narrow pusher slightly to contact the tile higher rather than slide its base; keep other tiles untouched.
Press the upper face of the same matching tile forward with a higher contact point to tip it over.
Follow the first matching tile's tilt with another gentle forward/down stroke.
Retract and lift the pusher to inspect the first tile and reposition without sweeping adjacent tiles.
Lower the closed pusher in front of the displaced matching tile, correcting the contact height before another tipping stroke.
Push at the upper half of the isolated matching tile with mostly horizontal motion to initiate tipping rather than press downward.
The first bamboo tile appears face up. Lift and retract before shifting to the adjacent matching bamboo tile.
Center the closed pusher on the second matching bamboo tile and lower to its upper face. The first is visibly face up.
Make a centered, mostly forward stroke on the second matching bamboo tile, avoiding the third and the nonmatching tiles.
Continue the second matching tile's forward tipping stroke with a small downward follow-through.
Lift and retract from the second bamboo tile to inspect its orientation and clear the row before moving laterally.
Two matching bamboo tiles are now face up. Align the narrow pusher with the third, keeping clear of the upright nonmatching tiles.
Tip the third matching bamboo tile forward with the closed narrow pusher; keep the adjacent nonmatching tiles upright.
Finish the third tile's tipping stroke, then lift away to inspect all three matching tiles.
All three matching bamboo tiles appear face up. Clear the right arm and begin a raised left-arm approach to the replacement-tile stack.
Approach the left stack from above while withdrawing the right arm within its own workspace.
Bring the open left gripper above the near tile on the left stack, keeping the right arm stationary and clear.
Descend slowly with the left gripper open around the near top tile of the replacement stack.
Close the left gripper on the replacement tile, then make a short lift to check visual retention.
The replacement tile is retained between the left fingers. Lift clear and begin rotating it toward a central handoff while staying on the left side.
Carry the retained replacement tile inward above the table while rotating toward a side-on handoff; maintain the left elbow-up branch.
Move the left-held tile to the central handoff pose and begin a high right-arm approach with gradual wrist rotation; keep both arms on their respective sides.
Hold the replacement tile steady in the left gripper while the open right gripper approaches above the row with continuous wrist rotation.
Continue the high right-arm approach and rotate toward the exposed face of the left-held replacement tile without contacting it yet.
Finish orienting the open right gripper above the handoff tile, keeping the left grasp steady.
Advance the open right fingers around the exposed portion of the left-held replacement tile for a controlled handoff.
Close the right gripper around the tile while the left continues supporting it; check alignment before releasing the left grip.
Release the left grasp and separate the arms slightly while keeping the right gripper closed; visually verify the tile follows the right hand.
The tile follows the right gripper. Carry it above the right workspace and begin rotating it upright; retract the empty left arm safely.
Corrected the rejected tensor; no prior motion occurred. Carry the retained tile rightward above the row and withdraw the left arm.
Continue carrying the tile toward the right end of the upright row, retaining it closed and maintaining overhead clearance.
Align the retained replacement tile just beyond the rightmost upright tile and finish its upright rotation while descending cautiously.
Lower the held replacement tile toward the table at the right end of the row, keeping its grasp closed and watching for contact.
Complete the short descent and open the right gripper to settle the replacement tile beside the rightmost tiles.
Withdraw the open right gripper upward and outward to inspect the released tile and avoid disturbing the upright neighbors.
Keep the gripper open and clear while the released tiles settle; inspect the right end for any needed correction.
The replacement tile has shifted forward of the row after release. Approach it from the clear outer side with open fingers for a position correction.
Center the open right fingers around the displaced face-up tile and descend slowly from the outer side.
Make a small final alignment and close the right gripper on the face-up tile for a corrective lift.
Lift the regrasped tile vertically with the right gripper closed, checking retention before correcting its upright orientation.
The tile is retained. Move inward with clearance and begin a gradual rotation from face-up to upright for accurate placement.
Continue the slow retained-tile rotation and inward overhead repositioning, preserving joint continuity.
Continue rotating the retained tile toward upright with small increments, keeping it clear of the table and row.
Use smaller rotation increments as the wrist turns, moving the held tile toward a clear upright-placement approach.
The rotation suffix was rejected near a wrist limit. Keep the grasp and orientation fixed while shifting inward to obtain a continuous safer approach.
Resume the upright rotation with smaller increments while moving inward enough to maintain wrist-limit margin and retain the tile.
Continue gradual upright rotation while moving inward and rearward to keep the wrist configuration continuous.
Finish the upright rotation over a clear area behind the right tiles, retaining the tile and avoiding the wrist limit.
Lower the now-upright retained tile over the clear table area, keeping the wrist orientation fixed and watching its base approach the surface.
Set the upright tile onto the clear table and release gently; this temporary support allows the near-limit wrist to be reoriented safely.
Retract the open right fingers from the supported tile, then begin unwinding the wrist away from its limit above the clear workspace.
